chapter: Los Angeles, Ellington and the recording scene
title: How Ellington's riffs and accidents shaped the band's sound
summary: Callender says band members set riffs that Duke wrote down, and that loose rehearsals with missing players created the "wild sounds".

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Well, a lot of things in the band came out of riffs, and the guys would set a riff and Duke would just write them down! Then the guys later got bitter because they didn't have brains enough to write them down.

Yeah, I'm sure that's where a lot of it came from. And sometimes Duke would put their names on it and sometimes Duke wouldn't put their names on it. That was sort of the way the band worked. And he took from those around him, and then those around him sometimes from him -- and that's the way it went.

Well, he was I guess the loosest bandleader there ever was. He didn't care... That's what I saw. If he had a bass player and a drummer, he'd start anyway. And I know a lot of the wild sounds came about that way. Like, maybe the third alto player or Johnny wouldn't be there, so the trombone, being in the register, although...you just change the clef sign, and it's the same thing. Somebody would take an alto saxophone part, and it would sound... You know, wild sounds! I know how they happened. A lot of
people figured it was on purpose, and sometimes it was just accidentally.
